title: return to castle wolfenstein
text: This is one of my all-time favourites and for me the best game in the Wolfenstein series. The story is that you play as Bj blazkowicz (you play as him in all of the games), you work for the O.S.A (office of secret actions) and you are to ruin the Nazis plans to bring back an ancient Germanic prince in hopes he will win the war for them, this also delves into the supernatural and horrific science themes, but at the end of the day the story matters least in this game. Wolfenstein has always been about mixing old with what’ new at the time so the old aspects in this are that: you collect health and armour, you carry all of your weapons at once, you run really quickly, and there are secret areas, other than scopes you fire from the hip. Then there are all of the newer elements such as actual objectives, stealth, a weapon handling system, and stamina. The levels are very diverse and you won’t be in the same looking area in a different section of the game again. The stealth is done  by destroying the alarms, slowly walking or crouching up on enemies and stabbing them with your knife, or you could shoot them with the silenced luger, the silenced sten or the silenced and thermal vision scoped m1 carbine. There are only two missions where stealth is mandatory, the rest you can go all guns blazing. There are a few things that replicate Wolfenstein 3d such as you can eat chicken just like in wolf 3d, there are plenty of secret areas where you’ll collect treasure just like in wolf 3d and you even start out in the same way (in your cell with a dead Nazi soldier only with a pistol and a knife), you have tons of weapons nearly all of them are war time weapons but two of them are: a mini-gun that liquefies people and a tesla gun, all of the machine guns (except for the mini-gun) are best used with controlled bursts to kill the enemies as quickly as possible. There are quite a few types of enemies in this game half of them you’ll find to be really annoying. This game does get increasingly difficult and I half to mention this one boss fight half way through the game is one of the highest difficulty spikes and one of the most annoying boss fights I’ve seen in a game. It’s a super solider (heavily armoured cyborg Nazi) who has a tesla gun (a gun that shoots an electric beam when they use it) so if he can see you he’s going to shoot you and it will drain your health pretty quickly and to make things worse the fight takes place in a very open area. Now that I mention that when you use the tesla gun it has a really short range, and it isn’t very accurate and it isn’t all that effective whereas when a super solider has one it’s a laser pointer that drains your health really quickly. Also near the end of the game the regular enemies will sometimes get stuck in this sort of staggering animation where it seems like they take very little damage, and for some reason on the second last mission the paratroopers seem to take much more damage than they can from the rest of the game. Other than that this remains one of my favourites and you should definitely play this game if you like old school shooters.

title: return to castle wolfenstein
text: Wait… I’m shooting at Nazis?  That’s not how I remember it…. It’s sixteen years old, showing its age, this is assuming you can get it to work on windows 10, which I personally hate on principle.  Though for a $1.56 who am I to complain?  The SS chicks make it a fun diversion, a throwback to a time when FPS games were maze-like, repetitive and needlessly hard… and for what it is, it’s still as perfectly serviceable as the Fuehrer’s bunker, sharing its vintage with the 2000 Deus Ex GOTY. I find myself not feeling nostalgic in the least, and I tell myself it could always be worse. Even at its worst, RTCW, even at full price is still less of a steaming turd than Duke Nukem Forever. $5 v $20, even if you bought a 4-pack of RTCW you’d still be getting your money’s worth, especially when compared to some of the newer Wolfenstein titles, which look really shiny and slick though seem horribly short and soulless if Old Blood is any indication. Return To Castle Wolfenstein surpasses old school Doom, and maybe even old school Quake, though in terms of nostalgia value, it’s only real competition is Serious Sam. What this Nazi-killing machine of a game lacks in polish it more than makes up for with character.  Then again… I haven’t even looked at Zombie Army Trilogy yet… The only downside is that it’s not 2001 anymore, and for a game of this calibre to not offer even partial controller support is an insult to common sense and beyond belief considering all the newer Wolfenstein titles are offering controller support, I have no choice but to view this as a potential negative that for me, ruined an otherwise perfectly serviceable retro title. Never mind my Razer Sabretooth Elite Gaming Controller, that cost $120 back in the day and at least that still works just apparently not with RTCW.  Damn shame, I was really looking forward to playing it too.  Guess I’ll just wait until New Order or Old Blood goes on sale for $1.24, and who knows, they might be♥♥♥♥♥♥ but at least I know they have controller support… Yes, I’m a sceptical steam convert, and thus far not overly impressed. If I have to wait for a sale to buy a game I may not even like at a reasonable price, then what’s the point when 80% of the time, retail would still be the same or cheaper than digital even with shipping from OS?!  I’m sorry, that doesn’t make any F@#!!#@ sense. Graphically it looks fine and I’m sure the game itself plays fine, not that I could be bothered.  This is to say nothing of the extremely odd and sometimes awkward screen resolution, even with much fiddling and adjusting. I suppose you could say I got my money’s worth, nearly 2-hours fiddling with the settings, actual gameplay time? 10 minutes, before uninstall. If you can put up with the keyboard and mouse only controls and the weird resolution issues, it’s less than the price of a cup of coffee and you could do a hell of a lot of worse for that price. By comparison Dinosaur Hunt is only 99 cents and it’s probably as much fun as watching paint dry but at least it has controller support and dinosaurs… Screw it. I can honestly recommend RTCW, though now I’m seriously considering Dinosaur Hunt because I know it’s so bad it will be hilarious and after 90 minutes of laughing at a 2015 game that looks and likely plays like a 2001 game in some strange way I’ll feel like I’ve offset my losses on Return To Castle Wolfenstein. I’m honestly starting to see why the Nazis lost the war…

title: revenge of the titans
text: Game: Revenge of the Titans Summary: A fun, somewhat unattractive tower defense game Rating (5/10 = failure): 8/10 Multiplayer: No Completion: 17 hrs Cards: Yes Cloud: Yes Cost:  ~1 USD bundled Oh wow, a story! It's mostly for kicks, but at least it gave me a reason to play (as sarcastic as that sounds, I actually mean it. I feel like there was a point to all that). The research system is fantastic. It may look daunting to the first-timer, but once I got used to it, I started to wish it was even bigger. As it is, it's good. While I'm sure it's meant as part of its aesthetics, the battle environments always look... sterile and off-putting. I would have liked to see some daytime areas, forests, cities. Maybe more weather effects like rain and snow outside of X-mas. Instead we get... rocks. And more rocks. In pale pastel colors. Add to that an ever-present, pointless dim spotlight effect which makes everything look dull and dim. On every stage. It's a fun game, but borderline unappealing and somewhat hard on the eyes. I'm not sure if I was playing it correctly, but I had difficulty setting up towers along paths, as creeps would invariably destroy those towers (not including the creeps that specifically go for towers). In any case, it didn't matter in the end, as I found that on most maps I could just make a super defense perimeter around the base and nothing would get past it except for boss monsters, in which case, all that required was a second set of towers attacking the boss right away. The automatic difficulty scaling could use some work. Once you get the hang of the game, you'll quickly start to rake in funds. But if you do too well (+50k in funds), the game gives you zilch next stage. It feels like it's punishing you for doing well, and even without looking it up, I could tell the game was "cheating" by doing that. Out of all the Puppygames, I regard this one as the best. It's not frustrating, it's not brutally hard, has a good length, several game modes, and even the stages I failed it didn't remain failed for long.

text: Well yet another mmo hits the market, the question being is this any better then the other ones. Riders Of Icarus uses mounts a great deal for the gameplay and questing. I do like the gameplay of this game, the classes feel different and each one is better for a spicific roll then the other. I like having the mounts in the game and they do fill alot of the gameplay but taming could take some points from other mmos, now its basicly based entirely on luck, theres just a few ways you can make it a bigger chance of success which is being higher level then the familiar and also you can buy in the shop taming success potions but that costs ellum which is slow to get if you decide not to buy for real money. Familiars are such a big deal in this game and i think they could do a better system for taming them, if you are taming example an elite you will have a pretty big chance of getting it but in the end game you tame the heroic mounts which the marks are really hard to get and when the system is pure luck its not really that fun experience, and the taming is exacly the same whatever grade familiar it is, common is the same as heroics in terms of taming, you just jump on. press one of W A S D now and then, then just hope you get it. Dont misstake me I enjoy the game but as said I think they can chance the system so its more about skill or something like that instead of pure luck.
